# dogfood: epic 005, its child task 062 and task 052 rebuilt from CLI calls alone,
# under fresh numbers: 001-auto-mail-mvp (epic), 002-auto-mail-walking-skeleton
# (its child) and 003-reflect-tool-hardening. Generated IDs are deterministic
# (AUTO_PLAN_SEED=1), so every later command names them literally.

auto plan init

# ---- 001: the epic ---------------------------------------------------------
# expect exit=0 stdout=new-epic.json
auto plan new auto-mail-mvp --kind epic
auto plan add 001 goal --title "Agents on one host address each other by name and get a reply" --description "Without knowing what session, pane, project or process the other one is."
auto plan add 001 goal --title "Mail is durable and at-least-once: it survives until explicitly acked" --description "The bus is for events nobody has to receive; mail is for messages someone must act on."
auto plan add 001 goal --title "A working agent learns it has mail in-band, at no cost when there is none"
auto plan add 001 goal --title "An idle agent is woken without corrupting a working one"
auto plan add 001 goal --title "Nothing in the MVP forecloses fan-out, leases or multi-host" --description "Schema you own is cheap to migrate; call sites you don't own are not."
auto plan add 001 journey --title "Sub-agent reports home" --description "Outcome: supervisor learns the child failed, in-band, without polling."
auto plan add 001 leg --actor supervisor --action "spawns an in-process sub-agent" --in j-bvmq
auto plan add 001 leg --actor sub-agent --action "hits a wall and mails #parent" --in j-bvmq
auto plan add 001 leg --actor supervisor --action "is nudged on its next tool call" --in j-bvmq
auto plan add 001 journey --title "Cross-project bug report" --description "Outcome: a fact discovered in one project reaches the project that owns it."
auto plan add 001 leg --actor "agent in project A" --action "finds a bug that belongs to project B" --in j-pn3v
auto plan add 001 leg --actor mail --action "persists it — nobody in B is running" --in j-pn3v
auto plan add 001 leg --actor "agent in project B" --action "is idle in a pane" --in j-pn3v
auto plan add 001 leg --actor "agent in project B" --action "reads, fixes, acks" --in j-pn3v
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Messages and events are immutable" --description "(functional) A message row is never updated after insert, and a delivery event is never rewritten. State changes are appended and re-projected."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Consumer state lives in a deliveries join, never on the message" --description "(functional) Read and ack state is keyed by (subscription, message), even though the MVP has exactly one subscription per address. That redundancy is the feature: fan-out becomes extra rows, competing consumers become a column."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Ack is a separate explicit call, from the first consumer" --description "(functional) Reading does not retire a message. Ack may do nothing but stamp a timestamp — no timer, no redelivery — but every consumer must call it."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Injected keystrokes are a fixed constant, into a verified agent" --description "(security) Two rules, both absolute. Content: the injected sequence is a fixed constant — an instruction to go and read mail — never interpolated from an envelope or body, or a sender would be typing into a stranger's pane."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Ack transitions exactly once and reports whether it won" --description "(functional) Ack is a conditional update inside the same transaction that appends its event, so concurrent acks on one delivery resolve to exactly one winner. The call returns which it was — a loser is told, never silently treated as success."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "At-least-once and unordered, as documented" --description "(functional) The MVP delivers exactly once, in order, by accident. The contract promises neither."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Addresses are virtual — no physical identity in them" --description "(functional) Physical identity (session, host, herdr/ntm pane) appears only as binding metadata, never in an address, never in a stored envelope's to field. Relative handles like #parent resolve at send time; the stored envelope always carries the resolved absolute address."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Sending to an address with no subscription persists, and a later subscriber sees it" --description "(reliability) The cross-project journey depends on both halves: mail sent to a project nobody is working in must persist, and the agent who subscribes tomorrow must receive it. A send reports two distinct counts — how many subscriptions exist (durable readers) and how many are currently bound (live agents) — because …"
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Hook environment capture stays an allowlist" --description "(security) Capture widens to reach herdr panes. It must stay a prefix allowlist and never become \"everything except known secrets\" — agent environments carry live credentials (this host's sessions expose a messaging token in plain env)."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "The nudge is free when there is no mail" --description "(operability) Notification runs in the agent's critical path on tool calls. The common case — no pending mail — must cost about what a stat costs, and must never be able to stall or break the hook."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Delivery never corrupts a working agent" --description "(functional) Intrusiveness escalates, never leads. Every message first waits for an in-band hook nudge; keystrokes are the last resort, firing only when the agent is idle by hook silence and the message has aged past a threshold."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Alpha: the store may be wiped, nothing may depend on it" --description "(compat) Event types and the store file carry an alpha marker. No upcasters, no migrations, no compatibility guarantee; reset is a supported operation."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "No session manager is hard-coded into stored data" --description "(compat) A binding records its physical target as an opaque (manager, target) pair — never a typed tmux_pane_id / herdr_pane_id column. Delivery goes through an effector interface with one implementation per manager."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "A capability is done when it passes end to end in the harness" --description "(operability) The guiding oracle is a harness scenario running the real auto binary in containers over real transports, with a realistic but minimal setup. Unit and package tests are supporting evidence, not the verdict — a task whose capability cannot be demonstrated end to end is not finished."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "The ontology lands before the code that uses it" --description "(functional) Canonical terms go into the ubiquitous-language glossary first, and then the same word is used everywhere — schema, event types, CLI, RPC methods, prose and commits. Naming is the one decision that propagates into every surface at once, including the ungreppable ones, so it cannot be tidied up afterwards."
auto plan add 001 rail --title "Nothing outside the mail package reads the store" --description "(operability) One client interface is the only API. The moment a skill or hook runs sqlite3 against the store, the schema is frozen and the transport swap is dead."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Mutable tables" --why "Two hosts' divergent mutable state is a conflict-resolution problem with no good answer."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Full CQRS with a projection process" --why "Rebuild tooling and eventual consistency for a few hundred rows a day."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Event-source the delivery lifecycle, not everything" --chosen "Append-only event log as the authority, projections maintained in the same transaction. Messages immutable." --why "Storage choice for a low-volume, debugging-heavy, eventually-distributed message store." --by agent --constrains g-w1fg --rejects a-ymt5 --rejects a-63s8
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A v1 prefix" --why "Implies v2 arrives alongside and obliges upcasters, a promise we do not want."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A docs-only alpha note" --why "Does not stop a skill matching on a bare type name."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Alpha marker in the type string and the store filename" --chosen "Prefix event types with `alpha` and name the store file with it. Carry a `version` integer on the envelope anyway." --why "Event sourcing makes the event vocabulary permanent, which raises the stakes on getting it right first time." --by agent --constrains g-w1fg --rejects a-57nj --rejects a-6tp0
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A bespoke socket protocol" --why "Rebuilds a solved problem."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Route mail over bus events only" --why "At-most-once broadcast cannot carry an ack." --wouldBreak r-jcvm
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Reuse auto-shared rpc + transport rather than a new wire" --chosen "Register `mail.*` methods on the existing JSON-RPC peer, alongside `doc.*`, `task.*`, `bus.*`. Notification rides the bus; operations ride RPC." --why "The MVP is single-host but must not foreclose multi-host." --by agent --constrains g-w1fg --rejects a-2gq9 --rejects a-pe53
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "RPC-first: route send/list/ack through the daemon" --why "Mail is down whenever the daemon is, and a failing agent must be able to post mail with nothing else alive."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "The MVP CLI writes the store directly; the daemon is never required" --chosen "`mail.Client` has two implementations. The **direct-store** one is what the MVP CLI binds to: send, list and ack work with no daemon running." --why "Seam 2 says send/list/ack are RPC calls, and D-3 registers `mail.*` on the daemon's peer — which would make the daemon the store's owner and put it in the path of every operation." --by agent --constrains g-gc8t --rejects a-2g81
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "auto mail letter …" --why "Coins a term, and the metaphor fights the channel/subscription model."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Qualify Message by context, as Event does" --why "The in-binary collision remains."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "No message resource noun on the CLI" --chosen "`auto mail` is itself the resource noun — flat verbs, no `message` subcommand. The glossary gains **Mail** (the stored unit, named `MAIL` in the schema), **Address**, **Subscription**, **Delivery** and **Binding** — the concepts the epic actually uses." --why "`docs/concepts/UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md` binds **Message** to a role-tagged exchange within a Session. A mail resource of the same name would make `auto search message get` and `auto mail message get` mean unrelated things in one binary." --by agent --constrains g-rbcw --rejects a-4kf4 --rejects a-m7rq
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Extend autowatch's Backend" --why "Wrong lifecycle: it abstracts sessions autowatch creates and owns, not panes created by herdr or ntm."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Hard-code herdr" --why "Breaks ntm panes, which hook capture already sees." --wouldBreak r-p2kk
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A general session-manager refactor across autowatch" --why "Large, speculative, and unused by this epic."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Mail's effector seam is separate from autowatch's execution Backend" --chosen "Leave that `Backend` untouched. Mail gets its own narrow effector seam — deliver to a pane, and ask whether it is alive — with one implementation per manager." --why "Three session managers are in play (ntm, tmux, herdr), with a long-term intent to consolidate on herdr. autowatch already has a `Backend` interface (`Start` / `Kill` / `SessionExists`) with a single tmux implementation." --by agent --constrains g-kqxw --rejects a-yxva --rejects a-f2m8 --rejects a-z90w
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Cron as the primary delivery path" --why "A latency floor, and the wrong shape even later."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "No notification at all" --why "Mail sits unread, the failure mode this epic exists to fix."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "The sender notifies inline; no cron sweep in the MVP" --chosen "On a single host the sender resolves the binding and notifies inline. The reconciling sweep — which is what heals dropped pushes — is deferred until there are pushes that can drop, i.e. multi-host." --why "A periodic inbox sweep was the obvious delivery driver, but a one-minute tick sets a 60-second floor on latency and burns work when nothing happened." --by agent --constrains g-kqxw --rejects a-kjh2 --rejects a-x13r
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Keep D-5 and accept best-effort escalation" --why "Silently breaks J2 and sits badly against G4's at-least-once promise." --wouldBreak r-vgcz
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "An in-memory timer only" --why "Lost on the daemon restarts this host is known for."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Inline notify for latency, plus a minimal reconcile tick for correctness" --chosen "Keep inline notification as the fast path, and add a **minimal reconcile tick** in the daemon that re-evaluates unacked mail against the escalation policy. autowatch already owns ticker/cron machinery, so this is small. The sweep is not a scheduler — it is the thing that makes escalation and the nobody-was-running case actually happen." --why "D-5 cut the sweep on the premise that on one host there are no pushes to drop. That premise does not survive contact with two facts." --by agent --constrains g-kqxw --rejects a-bcs8 --rejects a-48t5 --supersedes d-hr0p
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A separate lock table" --why "A second thing to keep consistent, and redundant: D-1's transaction already makes ack atomic."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Ack as an unconditional write" --why "Cannot tell a winner from a loser, which is the whole point." --wouldBreak r-apsc
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Broadcast delivery, with ack as a compare-and-set" --chosen "Each subscription holds its own `deliveries` row and its own ack, so two *subscriptions* never contend. Ack is a conditional update inside the existing append-and-project transaction (`WHERE acked_at IS NULL`), and **returns whether this call was the one that transitioned it**." --why "Q-1 settled fan-out as broadcast, and raised ack atomicity." --by agent --constrains g-gc8t --rejects a-y361 --rejects a-vrqj
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Keys immediately on idle" --why "Spends the most dangerous mechanism on the most ordinary case." --wouldBreak r-01p5
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Opt-in per subscription only" --why "The cross-project journey silently does nothing for anyone who did not know to opt in."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Escalating intrusiveness: nudge first, keystrokes last" --chosen "Notification escalates in stages. Every message first waits for an in-band hook nudge." --why "Q-2 rejected default-on keystroke injection in favour of escalation." --by agent --constrains g-kqxw --rejects a-6z14 --rejects a-aw9y
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "An enforced project/name shape" --why "Breaks addresses that are not about a project, like a swarm channel."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "A strictly opaque token with separators rejected" --why "The one variant that would foreclose prefix filtering."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Addresses are free-form; structure is convention, filtering is v2" --chosen "An address is an opaque string with no enforced structure and no required project segment. Validation is permissive but must **explicitly allow a separator character**, so hierarchical names remain expressible by convention and prefix filtering stays buildable later." --why "Q-3 chose flexibility over an enforced namespace, with prefix filtering deferred." --by agent --constrains g-rbcw --rejects a-dsj8 --rejects a-bt89
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Eager delivery rows at send time" --why "Silently breaks J2: the failure only appears when a subscriber arrives late." --wouldBreak r-q6hs
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Backfill from subscription time only" --why "Breaks J2 for the same reason, just less visibly." --wouldBreak r-q6hs
auto plan add 001 decision --title "Subscriptions backfill unacked history from a cursor" --chosen "The address holds the mail; a subscription holds a `from_cursor` and its ack state, and delivery rows are materialised **lazily on read**. A new subscription defaults to seeing all unacked mail on the address from the beginning, and can opt to start from now." --why "G2 keys consumer state by (subscription, message). If delivery rows were created eagerly at send time, a subscription created *later* would have none — and J2 leg 3, where an agent in project B reads mail sent before it existed, could never happen." --by agent --constrains g-gc8t --rejects a-djp7 --rejects a-txje
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Env promotion (AUTO_MAIL_SELF → AUTO_MAIL_PARENT)" --why "Bootstrap hole: a supervisor that subscribes mid-session cannot set a variable in its own running process."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "Launch-time stamping by herdr/ntm/delegate in the MVP" --why "Makes panes work too, but adds a cross-tool dependency this epic does not otherwise carry."
auto plan add 001 decision --title "#parent covers in-process subagents only, resolved from hook-supplied parentage" --chosen "`#parent` resolves from the parentage already carried on an in-process subagent's hook events — the parent's `session_id` alongside the child's `agent_id`. A hook records which agent is currently active for a session so the mail CLI can identify itself, since the hook payload never reaches a tool call and an in-process subagent shares the parent's …" --why "Q-4, answered in-process only." --by agent --constrains g-rbcw --rejects a-pesp --rejects a-2nmm
auto plan add 001 question --title "Two subscribers on one channel: a copy each, or compete for it?" --status answered --recommended "a copy each (broadcast)." --answer "Copy all messages to everyone. An important thing to include though — ack must be atomic. If two agents read the same message, then they race to ack it, only one must succeed. SQLite transaction should back ack. We push to the event log and maybe update a separate lock table."
auto plan add 001 question --title "Is keystroke injection on by default in alpha, or opt-in per subscription?" --status answered --recommended "on by default, with a per-subscription ceiling available." --answer "Agreed, we should be careful and escalate our intrusiveness. Start with hook injection, only use injection as a last resort."
auto plan add 001 question --title "Is the address namespace hierarchical, and is the project segment meaningful?" --status answered --recommended "hierarchical, purpose-based, with the leading segment conventionally a project id but never enforced." --answer "Leave it flexible. Virtual addresses can be anything, but we have prefix-based filtering as an option. Could be a v2 feature to be honest as I can't see a use for it right now."
auto plan add 001 question --title "Which spawn shapes does #parent cover, and how does the CLI identify which agent it is?" --status answered --recommended "in-process only for the MVP." --answer "In-process only."
# checkpoint 1

auto plan add 002 goal --title "One client seam: mail.Client is the only API, and the direct-store implementation needs no daemon"

auto plan add 002 ac --proves g-w1fg --title "G3 — ack is a separate explicit call; reading does not retire" --gwt "**Given** one unacked mail; **When** `auto mail list` is run twice with no `ack` between them; **Then** the mail is returned **both** times" --verify-cmd "(cd auto-mail && go test ./conformance/ ./internal/cli/)" --verify-tests auto-mail/conformance/conformance_test.go --verify-tests auto-mail/internal/cli/cli_test.go --discharges 001:r-jcvm
auto plan add 002 ac --proves g-w1fg --title "G13 / D-7 — ack transitions exactly once and reports whether it won" --gwt "**Given** one delivery row and N=16 goroutines calling `Ack` on it concurrently under `-race`; **When** they all complete; **Then** exactly **one** returns `wonTransition: true` and the other fifteen return `wonTransition: false`" --verify-cmd "(cd auto-mail && go test -race ./internal/cli/ ./internal/store/)" --verify-tests auto-mail/internal/store/store_test.go --verify-tests auto-mail/internal/cli/cli_test.go --discharges 001:r-apsc

auto plan add 002 ac --proves g-w1fg --title "G6 — send with no subscription persists, and reports both counts" --gwt "**Given** an address nobody has subscribed to; **When** `auto mail send --to <address> --message …` runs; **Then** it exits **0**, the mail is persisted, and the payload reports `\"subscriptions\": 0, \"bound\": 0`; **Given** a subscription exists but has **no binding row** (in T1 `bound` counts binding rows, not liveness — nothing refreshes `last_seen` until T3, per D-062-2); **Then** the payload reports `\"subscriptions\": 1, \"bound\": 0` — the two counts are distinct and mean different things to a sender" --verify-cmd "(cd auto-mail && go test ./conformance/) && (cd harness && uv run pytest tests/mail_flow -v)" --verify-tests auto-mail/conformance/conformance_test.go --verify-tests harness/tests/mail_flow/test_mail_loop.py --discharges 001:r-q6hs
auto plan add 002 ac --proves g-bvmq --title "G8 — the nudge is free when there is no mail, and can never break the hook" --gwt "**Given** any state of the mailbox; **When** `auto hooks fire --agent claude` processes a PostToolUse payload; **Then** the mail check performs **zero** store opens on **either** path — present flag or absent — asserted with a counting store-opener injected over the package var, and stats at most one path; **Given** pending mail; **Then** the hook emits exactly **one** `hookSpecificOutput` JSON object on stdout whose `additionalContext` names `auto mail list`, on `PostToolUse` events only — and when a hint rule also matches, both fragments ride that single emission …" --verify-cmd "(cd auto-mail && go test ./mail/) && (cd auto-cli && go test ./cmd/auto/) && (cd harness && uv run pytest tests/mail_flow -v)" --verify-tests auto-mail/mail/mail_test.go --verify-tests auto-cli/cmd/auto/hooksmail_test.go --verify-tests harness/tests/mail_flow/test_mail_loop.py --discharges 001:r-1eyq

auto plan add 002 alternative --title "Exit non-zero on a lost ack race" --why "A shell would treat a correct, expected outcome as a failure."

auto plan add 002 decision --title "Losing an ack race is a reported outcome, not an error exit" --chosen "`auto mail ack <id>` always prints `{\"id\":…, \"acked\":true, \"wonTransition\":<bool>}` on stdout and exits **0** when the delivery exists. A loser gets `wonTransition:false` plus a one-line note on stderr naming who won it." --why "G13 requires that a losing ack be \"told, never silently treated as success\". That fixes the payload, not the exit code, and the project convention reserves fail-fast exits for invalid CLI usage." --by agent --constrains ac-0f9w --rejects a-4kf4 --rejects a-m7rq
